text:
sophie_sales: URGENT help needed 50 SparkPayments POC is spiking 429s on /v1/tokenize right before the C-suite demo in 35m. Browser shows "429 Too Many Requests" and their frontend logs reference request-id rqt_sp_55e. They tried retries from the client and hit the same error.

raj_se: Which tenant are they on and do you have response headers? Any chance they are running parallel tokenization per keystroke?

sophie_sales: tenant=spark-payments-poc. Header snapshot: X-RateLimit-Limit: 150/min X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 Retry-After: 4 X-Request-ID: rqt_sp_55e. They reported a QA script that opened 70 parallel tabs during warmup.

diego_engineer: OK. Short term options: (A) temporary tenant burst for demo, (B) route demo to a smaller-model tokenization endpoint, (C) throttle at edge with WAF rules. Fastest is A. Ops, can you apply a 30m burst if approved?

ops_oncall: I can apply `POST /internal/admin/tenants/spark-payments-poc/burst {"minutes":30,"qps":450}`. Need SE/eng ack. cluster-zeta free_nodes=0 last_deploy=stable@2026-12-22T14:02Z.

raj_se: I approve burst. Also prepare a two-line client fix to send them: set max concurrency=6 and exponential backoff with jitter. I'll paste a code snippet after this message.

infra_bot: [autoscaler] cluster-zeta free_nodes=0 avg-latency=132ms recent_alerts=none

ops_oncall: Burst applied for 30m. OPS ticket OPS-1412 created. Watching ingress logs for rqt_sp_55e.

diego_engineer: Tailing ingress logs now. Found entries showing bucket exhaustion then success after burst apply:
```
[INGRESS] 2026-12-22T14:18:03Z tenant=spark-payments-poc req=rqt_sp_55e route=/v1/tokenize status=429 reason=bucket_empty concurrent=68
[INGRESS] 2026-12-22T14:18:05Z tenant=spark-payments-poc req=rqt_sp_55e route=/v1/tokenize status=200 lat_ms=98
```

sophie_sales: Demo resumed and leadership walkthrough completed. Customer asked about guaranteed capacity for peak checkout windows and enterprise pricing for spike protection.

lina_security: Also flagged: the customer wants confirmation on tokenization flow and whether PANs touch Redwood. Please open a separate security thread with their questionnaire and flow diagram. We'll need to provide SOC2 and PCI scoping summary.

raj_se: Post-demo action items: (1) send client concurrency + backoff snippet to the customer (snippet prepared), (2) follow-up call to propose Reserved QPS vs Dedicated (I'll draft two proposals), (3) offer a one-week Dedicated trial for peak validation, (4) add a QA note: do not run >20 parallel tabs during demos.

diego_engineer: Engineering follow-ups: add a console quick-action for demo-burst (with audit trail), publish a short runbook for sales (how to request bursts and expected timeline), and add a telemetry flag to detect demo-like bursts for proactive outreach.

ops_oncall: Burst will auto-revoke at T+30m. OPS-1412 remains open for quota review. I'll keep monitoring until T+35m then close.

sophie_sales: Thanks team 52 customer loved the demo. Scheduling the pricing/security follow-up for next week. Closing this thread now. :thumbsup:
